minor.issue: structured sent as a JSON STRING with NO category is not linked. category() only inspects dict structured, returns 'other', and subjects() yields nothing. ids_from_text then only looks at fields/full_text. Repro: result={'structured': json.dumps({'customer':{'piva':'22222222222'}})} gives no link. Fix: parse a JSON-string structured in category() as well (reuse the structured() parsing).

The fields/full_text fallback runs only when NO structured subject has an identifier. If structured has the supplier P.IVA (not a client) but the customer has only a name, a field 'P.IVA cliente: 22222222222' is ignored and there is no link. Consider always merging ids_from_text results; the ambiguity rule still protects against 2 different clients.

Combined label values such as 'P.IVA/CF: 22222222222' normalise to 'PIVACF22222222222' and don't match. The prefix regex lacks a PIVACF / PARTITAIVACF variant. A fallback could extract a lone 11-digit/16-char id from the string.
The 'category' returned to the UI is the raw res.category (e.g. 'Fattura' or missing → 'other'), not core.category(res). It is cosmetic but inconsistent with the normalisation used for linking.

critical_code_review_comments: Feed lookup: deleted clients/revoked tokens correctly 404. Tokens are only sha256-hashed and token_urlsafe(32) gives 43 chars. Hashes aren't indexed; add indexes on users.calendar_feed.hash and clients.calendar_feed.hash for public feed lookups at scale.
match_client returns the first client matching on piva OR cf. If one subject's P.IVA matches client A and its CF matches client B, only A counts, so the ambiguity check misses it (edge case).
The PDF includes overdue confirmed deadlines (all confirmed with due_date). That's fine, but consider labelling past dates.
Python slug truncates to 60 chars, JS slug doesn't, so the frontend filename can differ from the Content-Disposition for long names (cosmetic).
